text:
erin.hr: FYI we converted Sam from contractor -> full-time on 2026-08-15. Sam says he still got a 1099 for the period Jan-Aug and is worried about double reporting / tax withholding. Can payroll confirm what will be on his year-end forms? cc @diego.payroll

diego.payroll: Thanks Erin. Short answer: if he was a 1099 contractor for Jan 1026Aug 14 and then on payroll from Aug 15, he'll receive a 1099-NEC for contractor payments and a W-2 for wages. Withholding only applies to the W-2 wages after conversion. We need to check our AP records and ensure no duplicate classification.

maria.tax: Two quick checks: 1) Were any contractor payments reported incorrectly as employee wages via payroll? 2) Any reimbursements that were grossed up? If we accidentally reported the same amount twice, we must correct before filing.

sam.engineer: I was paid via vendor invoices as 1099 up to Aug 14, then got salary on Aug 15 onward. I didn't receive any reimbursements. I did notice one Sept bonus that shows under "Contractor Expenses" in Concur; not sure if that's rolled into payroll.

diego.payroll: Can you paste the invoice IDs or amounts? I'll reconcile. Also switching classification mid-year can create state withholding pro-rate issues depending on states worked. Which state were you in Jan-Aug?
sam.engineer: CA Jan-Aug, then moved to OR before hire on Aug 15. Now living in OR.
maria.tax: That matters. CA source income (1099) and OR wages (W-2) are OK, but we need to ensure state tax withholding and unemployment reports reflect the change. For the 1099, the vendor team should have issued a 1099-NEC to your home address on file. For W-2, withholding should be Oregon only after hire date.
diego.payroll: Reconciliation results (draft):
````
- 1099 payments recorded: $28,400 (Jan-Aug)
- W-2 wages paid: $24,800 (Aug 15-Dec)
- Potential mispost: Bonus $1,200 flagged in Concur under contractor expenses (Sep)
````
If that $1,200 was paid through payroll as a bonus, it's W-2; if it went to the vendor system, it's 1099. I'm opening a ticket with AP to trace payment path.

erin.hr: Action: Sam please confirm if you received vendor payment for that $1,200 or a payroll stub showing it. Also attach your W-4 and state withholding forms submitted at hire.
sam.engineer: I have a bank deposit on 2026-09-10 labelled "Vendor Pmt 4582" for $1,200. So that looks contractor. I also have payroll stubs and my W-2 stub for Dec.
maria.tax: Good find. That implies 1099 covers $29,600 and W-2 stays $24,800. No duplicate reporting. Next: payroll should ensure no state withholding taken for CA on the W-2 wages, and AP must confirm 1099 issued with our EIN and mailed. If any 1099 amounts were incorrectly reported under payroll, we issue corrected forms (W-2c or 1099 correction) before year-end.
diego.payroll: I'll: 1) confirm AP mailed 1099-NEC; 2) confirm W-2 state boxes (OR only); 3) check unemployment reports for CA for the 1099 period. ETA EOD 2 business days.
payroll-bot: Case logged PR-3097. Assigned diego.payroll. Remind: employee to keep records for filing estimated taxes if needed.
erin.hr: Thanks all. Sam, HR will send a short note you can attach to your tax file explaining the mid-year status change.
sam.engineer: Appreciate it 44d
